transcript: We Live In Cairo is a new musical at New York Theatre Workshop about a group of student activists in the midst of Arab Spring. The show is about revolution and resistance and features an ensemble cast and a wonderful onstage band. In Act 1 we’re introduced to the different characters and we see some events leading up to January 25th 2011 which brought a massive protest to Tahrir Square in Cairo. Act 2 follows the aftermath and the revolution is continued to evolve. For a second preview, I thought this was in great shape. It dragged a little bit during Act 1 and some of the staging felt clunky, but nothing that can't be tightened up. The cornerstone of the show is the music which is lovely. The Middle Eastern infused orchestrations and vocal arrangements are really cool and this is definitely one of the most exciting new scores I've encountered in a while — I would love a cast recording. We Live In Cairo is running at New York Theatre Workshop through late November. With that, another program for my collection.
